## (4) Regenerate vs recompute — the decision
Chose REGENERATE-ON-A-SCHEDULE (recompute-and-commit; the runner reads the committed table at each fuse read). Not recompute-at-read, because (a) untracked/runs/ is host-local and gitignored — it does not survive a fresh clone, so a recompute-at-read fuse would have no population and a different threshold on every host, breaking reproducibility; (b) reading hundreds of records + sorting on every dispatch is pure overhead for a threshold that moves by seconds per new run; (c) staleness is detectable (the recompute prints the delta) rather than silent; (d) the ruling demands the published table BE the source. The runner parses the committed machine block (<!-- BEGIN harness-p95 --> ... ```json ... <!-- END harness-p95 -->) and falls back to hardcoded constants ONLY when the table is unreadable (degraded/bare tree).
